items.prompt: Which word starts the first step in instructions?
hints: Instructions go in order.
Think about the very start.
Which word means number one?
items.explanation: First starts the first step. Next and then come in the middle, and finally comes last.

options.why: Next comes after the first step.
Then comes after the first step.

hints: Look at the first word of each step.
The time words go First, Next, Then, Finally.
Start with the step that begins with First.
items.explanation: The time words show the order: first, next, then and finally.
items: Next, put toothpaste on the brush.
Then brush all of your teeth.
Finally, rinse your mouth with water.

items.prompt: Write a recount of something you did last weekend. Write at least three sentences.
hints: Start with when and where.
Use first, then and after that.
End with how you felt.
items.explanation: A recount tells real events in the order they happened. It uses past tense verbs and time words.

criteria.label: Tells what happened in order
Uses past tense verbs, like went and played
Capital letters and full stops
Uses time words, like first, then and after that

planning: What happened first, next and last?
items.model: Last Saturday, I went to the beach with my family. First, we built a sandcastle. Then we swam in the sea. After that, we ate fried rice under a tree. I felt happy and tired when we went home.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best start for a recount?
hints: A recount tells about something that really happened to you.
It says when and where.
Look for a sentence about the past that says when and who.
items.explanation: A recount starts by saying when, where and who. Last Sunday, I went to the zoo with my family does that.

options.why: This is a step in instructions.

options.text: Last Sunday, I went to the zoo with my family.

options.why: This is a fact, not a recount.

options.text: Once upon a time, a lion was sad.
options.why: This is the start of a story.

items.prompt: Write instructions for washing your hands. Use first, next, then and finally.
hints: Think about washing your hands right now.
Start each step with a time word.
Then add a bossy verb, like wet or rub.
items.explanation: Instructions use time words and bossy verbs so the reader can follow each step.

criteria.label: Steps are in the right order
Uses first, next, then and finally
Each step starts with a bossy verb, like wet or rub
Capital letters and full stops

items.model: First, wet your hands with water. Next, rub soap all over your hands. Then scrub between your fingers and under your nails. Finally, rinse your hands and dry them with a clean towel.

items.prompt: Recounts are about the past. Which sentence fits a recount?
hints: A recount tells what already happened.
Look at the doing words.
Which doing word is in the past?
items.explanation: Ate is the past of eat, so We ate noodles for dinner fits a recount.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best last step for planting a seed?
hints: The last step comes at the end.
Look at the first word of each choice.
Which time word means last?
items.explanation: Finally shows the last step: put the pot in a sunny place.

options.text: Finally, put the pot in a sunny place.
Once upon a time, there was a seed.
options.why: This is how a story starts.

items.prompt: Describe your favourite place. What can you see, hear and smell there?
hints: Close your eyes and picture the place.
Write one sentence for each sense.
items.explanation: Good description uses the senses and describing words, so the reader can picture the place.

criteria.label: Names the place
Uses at least three describing words
Writes about two or more senses
Capital letters and full stops

items.model: My favourite place is my grandma's kitchen. I can see big pots and bright green vegetables. I can hear oil sizzling in the pan. It smells of garlic and sweet fried bananas. It is warm, busy and happy.

hints: Look at the time words.
Morning comes before lunchtime.
Evening comes last.
items.explanation: The time words show the order: in the morning, then, at lunchtime and in the evening.
items: In the morning, we packed a picnic.
Then we drove to the beach.
At lunchtime, we ate our sandwiches.
In the evening, we went home tired and happy.

items.prompt: Read the start of the story. Write what happens next and how it ends. 'Tika found a tiny key in the sand. She looked around. Then she saw a little wooden box.'
hints: Start with what Tika does with the key.
Decide what is inside the box.
Finish with how Tika feels.
items.explanation: A good ending follows on from the start, solves the mystery and finishes clearly.

criteria.label: The story follows on from the start
Has a clear ending
Uses joining words: and, but, so, because
Capital letters and full stops

items.model: Tika picked up the box and tried the key. It turned with a click! Inside, there was a shiny shell and a note. The note said, 'Keep this safe for the next person.' Tika smiled. She added her own shell to the box and buried it again for someone else to find.

items.prompt: Which title is best for a recount about a farm trip?
hints: A recount tells about something you did.
Look for a title about a real trip.
Which title sounds like it tells what you did?
items.explanation: Our trip to the farm tells the reader this is a recount of a real trip.

options.why: This sounds like a fact text.
This sounds like a made-up story.

items.prompt: Write a thank-you note to someone who helped you.
hints: Start with Dear and the name.
Say what they did and why it helped.
items.explanation: A thank-you note says who it is for, what you are thankful for and who it is from.

criteria.label: Starts with Dear and a name
Says thank you and what for
Ends with From and a name
Capital letters and full stops

items.model:
Dear Aunt Mira,
Thank you for helping me fix my bike. Now I can ride to the park with my friends. You are very kind.
From Rafi

items.prompt: Which sentence is the most interesting?
hints: Interesting sentences have details.
Look for describing words.
Which sentence helps you picture it?
items.explanation: Tiny, brown and round and round help us picture the puppy.

options.why: This is correct, but it has few details.

options.text: The tiny brown puppy chased its tail round and round.

hints: Two sentences are right.
A bossy sentence tells you what to do.
Which ones start with a doing word?
items.explanation: Cut the bread and Wash your hands tell you what to do. They start with bossy verbs.

items.prompt: Write instructions for making a fruit salad. Start with a list of what you need.
hints: Write the list first, with commas.
Use first, next, then and finally.
Knives are sharp, so ask an adult to help.
items.explanation: Instructions list what you need first. Then they give clear steps in order.

criteria.label: Has a list of what you need, with commas
Steps in order with time words
Each step starts with a bossy verb
Asks an adult to help with cutting

items.model:
You will need: a banana, a mango, some grapes, a bowl and a spoon.
First, wash the fruit. Next, ask an adult to help you cut the banana and the mango. Then put all the fruit in the bowl. Finally, mix it gently with a spoon and enjoy!

items.prompt: Look at the pictures. Write a recount of a class trip to a farm.

figure.alt: Four pictures joined by arrows: a bus, a farm, a cow and a house.

hints: Start with when the trip was.
Write about each picture in order.
End with how the day felt.
items.explanation: A recount tells the events in order. The pictures show the order: bus, farm, cows, home.

criteria.label: A sentence or more for each picture
Past tense verbs
Time words to show the order
Capital letters and full stops

planning: What did you see and do at the farm?
items.model: On Monday, our class went on a trip to a farm. We rode there on a big yellow bus. At the farm, we fed the cows and watched the hens. In the afternoon, we got back on the bus and went home. It was a brilliant day.

items.prompt: Write a short story with a problem and a happy ending. Use at least two joining words.
hints: Plan the problem first.
Use because or so to explain what happens.
Finish with a happy ending.
items.explanation: A good story has a clear problem that gets solved. Joining words help link the ideas.

criteria.label: Has a beginning, a problem and an ending
Uses two joining words: and, but, so, because
Uses past tense verbs
Capital letters, full stops and other end marks

planning: How does everyone feel at the end?
items.model: One morning, Bayu's little cat, Kiki, climbed up the mango tree. She was stuck, and she cried, 'Meow!' Bayu could not reach her because the branch was too high. So he ran to get his dad. Dad brought a ladder and lifted Kiki down gently. Bayu gave her a big hug. 'No more climbing!' he laughed.
